analysis.explanation: The Random Forest classified this binary as MALWARE with probability 0.9550, and all 20 top SHAP features push toward cryptojacking (+0.0059 to +0.0112), with no opposing features in the list. The strongest signal is a cluster of arithmetic and bit-rotation n-grams: SUB SBB (+0.011155), ADD ROR (+0.010317), MOV ROL (+0.008837), SUB ADC (+0.008215), ROR ROL (+0.006815), ADC SUB (+0.006686), XOR ADC (+0.006533), MOV ADC (+0.006431), ROL MOV (+0.006352), SBB INC (+0.005953) and CMP SHLD (+0.005905). Rotates, carry-propagating add/subtract and shifts-with-double-precision are typical of hash and cipher inner loops and multi-precision arithmetic, which are the computational core of proof-of-work mining. A secondary group of stack and control-flow n-grams (MOVZX PUSH, ADD PUSH, PUSH RET, ADD POP, CMP PUSH, POP PUSH, CALL PUSH, POP TEST) suggests dense call/return sequences and possibly obfuscated or unusual control flow, which fits packed or hand-tuned code. INC INC has a high frequency (0.023190) and also contributes positively, though it is a weak, generic pattern on its own. The evidence supplies no function names, API calls or strings, so the conclusion rests on mnemonic-level statistical patterns only. Because many independent features agree and the model's probability is high, I assess this as high-confidence, with the caveat that crypto-like instruction mixes can also occur in legitimate cryptographic libraries, so confirmation through dynamic or string analysis is advisable.

evidence_analysis.assessment: Top feature. Subtract followed by subtract-with-borrow is a multi-word arithmetic idiom common in big-number and hash computation, consistent with mining kernels.

Addition followed by right rotate is characteristic of hash round functions (e.g. SHA-style or similar mixing steps). The very low frequency (0.000189) but high SHAP suggests a concentrated, distinctive occurrence.
Zero-extending byte loads followed by pushes suggest byte-level data handling and stack-heavy code; a weaker indicator, but the high frequency (0.002451) makes it influential.
Loading a value then rotating left matches cipher/hash round operations; frequency of 0.002828 suggests repeated use.
Arithmetic followed by a stack push; generic on its own, but contributes as part of the unusual stack-manipulation profile.
Mixed subtract/add-with-carry sequence indicative of multi-precision arithmetic, supporting a compute-heavy numeric kernel.
A push immediately before a return is an uncommon pattern in compiler output and can indicate return-address manipulation, obfuscation or hand-written assembly.
Stack-adjustment idiom; contributes as part of the atypical stack/control-flow profile, not specific to mining.
Compare followed by push; generic control-flow-adjacent pattern with modest, supportive value.
Pop immediately followed by push suggests register shuffling or thunk-like code, possibly obfuscation or hand-optimized routines.
Adjacent opposite-direction rotates are unusual and strongly associated with bit-mixing in cryptographic primitives.
Carry-propagating arithmetic followed by subtraction; reinforces the multi-precision arithmetic theme.
XOR combined with add-with-carry is typical of mixing steps in hash and stream-cipher routines.
Moves feeding carry-add operations at frequency 0.001131 indicate repeated arithmetic with carry propagation.
Call followed by push is a common prologue pattern; weak individually but consistent with the dense call structure of the sample.
Rotate followed by move, again matching round-function style bit manipulation and complementing MOV ROL.
Pop followed by a test is a generic epilogue/branch pattern; low specificity, contributes to the overall profile.
Highest frequency (0.023190) among the listed n-grams. Consecutive increments suggest pointer or counter advancement in tight loops; non-specific but consistent with iterative compute loops.
Borrow-subtract followed by increment, tying into the multi-precision arithmetic cluster.
Double-precision shift following a compare is uncommon in general code and is associated with wide-integer arithmetic and bit-manipulation in crypto routines.
